2026-12-29.title: 29 December · Fifth Day within the Octave of Christmas
readings: Whoever loves a brother or sister lives in the light
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice
A light for revelation to the Gentiles
2026-12-29.alt: Optional memorial: St Thomas Becket, bishop and martyr. Liturgical colour: white.
2026-12-29.verse: Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.
theo: Old Simeon, “righteous and devout, looking forward to the consolation of Israel”, had been promised by the Holy Spirit that he would not die before seeing the Lord's Messiah. Guided by the Spirit he comes into the Temple just as Mary and Joseph bring in the child. He takes Jesus in his arms and sings the Nunc Dimittis, which the Church prays every night at Compline: now I can die in peace, for I have seen your salvation.

Simeon's song is universal: the child is “a light for revelation to the Gentiles” as well as the glory of Israel. But he also speaks of contradiction: the child will be “a sign that will be opposed”, and a sword will pierce Mary's soul. The first reading draws the practical lesson: “whoever says, ‘I abide in him,’ ought to walk just as he walked”; whoever loves a brother or sister lives in the light. St Thomas Becket, archbishop of Canterbury, killed in his cathedral on this day in 1170, gave his life defending the freedom of the Church.
outline: Ask: what are you waiting for in life? Simeon waited for one thing.
Simeon comes at the right moment.
Christ divides hearts; the sword pierces Mary.
live: Pray Simeon's song before sleeping tonight.
Make peace with someone you have avoided.
2026-12-29.prayer: Lord, now let your servant go in peace; your word has been fulfilled. My eyes have seen the salvation you prepared for all peoples. Let me walk in your light and love my brothers and sisters. Amen.
altar: Like Simeon, at each Mass we receive Christ into our arms and hearts. Our eyes have seen his salvation.

quick: Simeon, led by the Spirit, holds the Saviour in his arms.
Christ is the light for all nations.
He is also a sign that will be opposed.
2026-12-29.action: Pray the Nunc Dimittis before sleeping tonight.
2026-12-29.question: Have my eyes truly seen the Lord's salvation this Christmas?

family.explain: Old Simeon waited all his life to see Jesus. When he held the baby, he was full of joy and peace.
family.intention: We pray for grandparents and all elderly people.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we learn from the old people in our family?”

pm.open: Lord, now you let your servant go in peace, for my eyes have seen your salvation. Lord Jesus, as we gather in this Christmas Octave, let us walk in your light. Amen.
share: John says whoever loves lives in the light (1 John 2:10). Is there someone I find hard to love?
Simeon waited all his life (Luke 2:25). What am I waiting for from God?
A sword will pierce your soul (Luke 2:35). How do joy and sorrow meet in my life?
pm.resp: Our eyes have seen your salvation.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a light to all nations.
For the elderly, that like Simeon and Anna they may find peace in God.
For the dying, that they may go in peace.
For those who hate, that they may come into the light of love.
For our group, that we may walk as Jesus walked.
pm.close: Lord God, Simeon saw your salvation in the Child Jesus. Let us walk in the light of love, and at the end of our lives go in peace to you. Amen.

illus: An old man in a hospice in Kottayam, after receiving Holy Communion on Christmas, said to the chaplain: “Now I can go in peace. I have seen him.” He died a few days later, smiling.

homily: Dear friends, on this fifth day of the Christmas Octave St John writes: by this we may be sure that we know him, if we obey his commandments. Whoever says, I abide in him, ought to walk just as he walked (1 John 2:3, 6). Knowing Christ is not only an idea; it is a way of walking.

John continues: whoever says, I am in the light, while hating a brother or sister, is still in the darkness. Whoever loves a brother or sister lives in the light (1 John 2:9–10). Christmas light is tested by love.

In the Gospel Mary and Joseph bring the infant Jesus to the Temple. There the old man Simeon, righteous and devout, who had been waiting for the consolation of Israel, takes the child in his arms and praises God: Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace, for my eyes have seen your salvation, a light for revelation to the Gentiles (Luke 2:25–32).

Simeon waited his whole life, and his waiting was fulfilled in holding a baby. The Church prays his song every night at Compline, before sleep. It is the prayer of one who is at peace because he has seen Christ.

But Simeon also tells Mary: this child is destined for the falling and the rising of many, and a sword will pierce your own soul too (Luke 2:34–35). The light of Christmas already points to the Cross. Love costs.

Let us ask for Simeon's patience and peace. Let us walk as Jesus walked, loving our brothers and sisters, so that we truly live in the light. And tonight, before sleep, let us pray: now, Lord, let your servant go in peace. Amen.
kids: Children, old Simeon held baby Jesus and was so happy! We hold Jesus in our hearts when we receive Him with love.

points.h: God carries us to the end
sub: God carries his people through sorrow.
q: even to your old age I am he, even when you turn gray I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear; I will carry and will save.

Then Simeon blessed them and said to his mother Mary, “This child is destined for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be opposed so that the inner thoughts of many will be revealed—and a sword will pierce your own soul too.”

concl: The waiting of Israel is fulfilled in Simeon's arms.
Let us walk in the light.
